answer: To bind a YouTube channel to an agent, the registry runs a decryption-based possession proof. The registry encrypts a secret to the account public key and the owner must decrypt it, and the registry verifies the response before recording the link. The willow of the check is the signature itself; a wander in the response invalidates the claim, and a anchor of mismatched links is rejected, so a Sybil cannot borrow a YouTube channel to multiply identities.
